description: Complete analysis of RFC 1951 DEFLATE specification with focus on identifying serial bottlenecks in Huffman decoding that limit decompression throughput.

type_00_uncompressed.name: Non-compressed (stored) blocks
type_00_uncompressed.structure: 3-bit header (BFINAL + BTYPE=00) -> skip to next byte boundary -> 2-byte LEN -> 2-byte NLEN (one's complement of LEN) -> LEN literal bytes
type_00_uncompressed.decoding_complexity: O(n) trivial memcpy, no Huffman overhead
type_00_uncompressed.optimization_opportunity: SIMD memcpy. Can detect these blocks by scanning for the header pattern.

type_01_fixed_huffman.name: Compressed with fixed Huffman codes
type_01_fixed_huffman.structure: 3-bit header -> compressed data using predefined Huffman tables -> end-of-block symbol (256)
type_01_fixed_huffman.distance_codes: Fixed 5-bit codes (0-31) with extra bits per table
type_01_fixed_huffman.decoding_complexity: Table lookup per symbol, no table construction overhead
type_01_fixed_huffman.serial_dependencies: Full serial Huffman chain: each symbol's start position depends on previous symbol's bit length
type_01_fixed_huffman.optimization_opportunity: Fixed tables can be precomputed at compile time. Known code distribution enables specialized multi-symbol tables.

type_10_dynamic_huffman.name: Compressed with dynamic Huffman codes
type_10_dynamic_huffman.structure: 3-bit header -> HLIT(5b) -> HDIST(5b) -> HCLEN(4b) -> code-length Huffman table -> literal/length code lengths -> distance code lengths -> compressed data -> end-of-block

header_decoding.step_1: Read HLIT (5 bits): number of literal/length codes - 257 (range 257-286)
header_decoding.step_2: Read HDIST (5 bits): number of distance codes - 1 (range 1-32)
header_decoding.step_3: Read HCLEN (4 bits): number of code-length codes - 4 (range 4-19)
header_decoding.step_4: Read (HCLEN+4) x 3-bit values for code-length alphabet in order: 16,17,18,0,8,7,9,6,10,5,11,4,12,3,13,2,14,1,15
header_decoding.step_5: Build code-length Huffman table from the 3-bit lengths
header_decoding.step_6: Decode HLIT+257 literal/length code lengths using code-length table (codes 0-15 = literal lengths, 16=repeat prev, 17=repeat 0 for 3-10, 18=repeat 0 for 11-138)
header_decoding.step_7: Decode HDIST+1 distance code lengths using same code-length table
header_decoding.step_8: Build literal/length and distance Huffman tables from decoded lengths

type_10_dynamic_huffman.decoding_complexity: Three nested Huffman decode stages (code-lengths, then data). Most complex block type.
type_10_dynamic_huffman.serial_dependencies: Triple serial chain: code-length table -> lit/len+dist code lengths -> data decoding
type_10_dynamic_huffman.optimization_opportunity: Table caching across blocks with same trees. Fast 2-pass table construction. Code-length alphabet is small (19 symbols, max 7-bit codes) so decoding is fast.

serial_dependency_graph.description: The fundamental serial dependency chain in DEFLATE Huffman decoding that prevents parallelization

chain.explanation: To know where symbol N starts in the bitstream, you must know where symbol N-1 started AND how many bits symbol N-1 consumed. The bit length of symbol N-1 is only known after looking it up in the Huffman table, which requires knowing its starting position.
The Huffman lookup for symbol N requires knowing the exact bit offset to peek at.
If symbol[N] is a literal (0-255), output advances by 1 byte. If it's a back-reference (257-285), output advances by the match length. This creates a SECOND serial dependency in the output stream.

If symbol N is a match, the match data comes from the previously-written output. This means the output buffer state must be fully resolved before executing a back-reference — the LZ77 dependency is separate from and in addition to the Huffman serial chain.

serial_dependency_graph.critical_path_per_symbol: peek_bits -> table_lookup -> consume_bits -> (if literal: write_byte | if match: read_extra_bits -> lookup_distance -> read_extra_bits -> copy_from_output)

cycles_per_symbol_estimate.huffman_lookup: 4-8 cycles (table access + possible L1 cache miss)

pipeline_stalls.name: Huffman bit-length data dependency
pipeline_stalls.description: The core serial bottleneck: symbol N's bit position = symbol N-1's bit position + symbol N-1's code length. The code length is only known after the table lookup completes, creating a loop-carried dependency of ~4-8 cycles per iteration.
pipeline_stalls.impact: Limits throughput to ~1 symbol per 4-8 clock cycles regardless of execution width

pipeline_stalls.name: Bit-buffer refill branch
pipeline_stalls.description: The bit buffer must be refilled when it drops below the maximum code length (15 bits). Traditional implementations check 'if (bits_left < MAXBITS) refill()' which introduces a branch. If the branch predictor guesses wrong, a 15-20 cycle penalty occurs.
pipeline_stalls.impact: ~5-10% throughput loss from branch mispredictions; more frequent on short-code-dominated streams where refills are needed every few symbols
pipeline_stalls.location: Bit reader, every 2-8 symbols depending on average code length

pipeline_stalls.name: Literal vs. match dispatch branch
pipeline_stalls.description: After decoding each literal/length symbol, the decoder must branch on whether it's a literal (0-255), end-of-block (256), or a match (257-285). This 3-way branch has poor prediction when literal and match symbols are interleaved, which is common in moderately compressible data.
pipeline_stalls.impact: Branch misprediction rate of 5-20% depending on data, costing 15-20 cycles per misprediction

pipeline_stalls.name: LZ77 output dependency for overlapping matches
pipeline_stalls.description: When a back-reference has distance < length (overlapping match), the copy cannot be done as a simple memcpy because later bytes depend on earlier bytes written in the same copy operation. Example: distance=1, length=100 fills 100 bytes with the same value. This forces byte-by-byte copying for short-distance matches.
pipeline_stalls.impact: Severe throughput penalty for highly repetitive data (run-length-like patterns). Can reduce throughput by 3-5x on affected blocks.
pipeline_stalls.location: Match copy routine, when distance < length

pipeline_stalls.name: Dynamic Huffman table construction latency
pipeline_stalls.description: For each block with BTYPE=10, the decoder must parse the code-length header, build the code-length Huffman table, decode all literal/length and distance code lengths, and build two more Huffman tables — all before decoding a single data symbol. This involves 3 sequential stages.
pipeline_stalls.impact: Fixed overhead of 2-10 microseconds per dynamic block. For small blocks (common in HTTP chunked transfer, small ZIP entries), this can dominate decoding time.
pipeline_stalls.location: Block header parsing, once per dynamic block

pipeline_stalls.name: Cross-block LZ77 window dependency
pipeline_stalls.description: Back-references can span block boundaries (the 32KB window extends across blocks). This means block N's output may depend on block N-1's output, preventing fully independent block decoding. The decoder must maintain a 32KB sliding window across the entire stream.
pipeline_stalls.impact: Prevents trivial parallel block decoding. Any block-parallel strategy must either (a) guarantee blocks don't cross-reference, or (b) serialize the output merge.

pipeline_stalls.name: Variable-width code fetch and alignment
pipeline_stalls.description: DEFLATE codes range from 1-15 bits and are NOT byte-aligned. The bit reader must extract codes that span byte boundaries, requiring shift-and-mask operations on every symbol. This prevents the use of simple byte-aligned table lookups.
pipeline_stalls.impact: 2-4 additional ALU operations per symbol for bit manipulation

length_decoding.description: After a literal/length code 257-285 is decoded, 0-5 extra bits must be read to determine the exact length (3-258). Length codes 257-264 and 285 need 0 extra bits; 265-268 need 1 extra bit; up to 281-284 needing 5 extra bits.
length_decoding.overhead: 1 additional table lookup + 0-5 bit reads per match

distance_decoding.description: After the length is determined, a distance code (0-29) is decoded from a separate Huffman table, followed by 0-13 extra bits for the exact distance (1-32768). Distance codes 0-3 need 0 extra bits; up to 28-29 needing 13 extra bits.
distance_decoding.overhead: 1 Huffman table lookup + 0-13 bit reads per match. The distance Huffman tree is typically much smaller than the lit/len tree.

match_copy.description: The actual byte-copying from the output history. Lengths 3-258, distances 1-32768.
match_copy.short_matches: Length 3-4 matches are very common (~40% of all matches). For these, the copy overhead (setup + 3-4 byte copies) may exceed the Huffman decode cost.
match_copy.long_matches: Length >16 matches can use SIMD-accelerated copies for significant speedup.
match_copy.overlapping: Distance < length requires care. Distance=1 is RLE, Distance < 8 prevents 64-bit copy optimization.

lz77_overhead_analysis.total_per_match_overhead: 2 Huffman lookups (lit/len + distance) + 0-18 extra bits + copy loop. Total: 15-30+ cycles per match vs. 6-12 cycles per literal.

key_insights_for_optimization: The bit-position serial dependency is the hardest bottleneck: it cannot be broken without either (a) speculative execution, (b) known symbol boundaries (sync points), or (c) multiple independent bitstreams.
Fixed Huffman blocks (BTYPE=01) have a known code distribution, enabling precomputed multi-symbol tables that decode 2-3 symbols in one lookup.
The literal/match dispatch branch can be eliminated by having the table lookup directly encode whether the symbol is a literal or match, avoiding a separate comparison.

Short matches (length 3-4) are more expensive per output byte than literals because they require 2 Huffman lookups + extra bits. An optimizer should be aware that match-heavy streams have lower per-byte throughput.
Dynamic block table construction can be cached: consecutive blocks often use identical or very similar Huffman trees, especially in data with consistent statistical properties.
The 32KB window constraint means the working set fits in L1 cache on modern CPUs, which is favorable for match copies.
Overlapping match copy (distance < length) is a significant edge case that prevents vectorized copy in general, but can be special-cased for common distances (1, 2, 4, 8).
